tier_reason: Tier stays C (later-fixed-bug cap). Caveat correction: the 6.4x and 6.9x figures compare against the original built without _ENABLE_AVX2; the fair figure against the AVX2 original is 2.8-3.9x, and the C++ multithread rows include thread creation and thread_local workspace allocation in the timed region.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Highway path vs the original AVX2 build: 2.8-3.9x (33.42 ms to 8.48 ms at 640x480 derived); the 6.4x/6.9x rows (269.72 vs 38.85 ms at 1280x960) run the original without _ENABLE_AVX2.
corrections.caveats: Self-baseline only; numbers predate the PR #383 crash fix; C++ MT rows time 28 thread creations and per-thread workspace allocation (128 iterations total) while the Rust harness warms workers and times after a barrier; libfacedetection_rs not on crates.io; Highway untested on ARM, no runtime dispatch.

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Caveat correction: the ImageMagick baseline runs a full-resolution Radon transform, not Hough, and Leptonica's deskew works on a 4x-reduced binary image with a limited +/-7 degree search, so the 30-40x is an algorithmic and resolution difference rather than a like-for-like implementation win.

corrections.caveats: ImageMagick DeskewImage = full-resolution Radon transform (MagickCore/shear.c); Leptonica sweeps a 4x-reduced binary image then refines at 2x; default search +/-7 degrees (#622, #644); silent no-op below 0.1 degree or confidence under 3.0; corners clipped; single 2014 anecdote, PR #61 closed unmerged; OCRmyPDF later dropped Leptonica for ABI reasons.

tier_reason: Tier stays C. Caveat correction: the headline pages/s is a tail-dominated metric (each track is smaller than one worker batch, so wall time is set by a few slow degraded pages), measured with unequal parallelism (8-48 Tesseract processes vs one EasyOCR GPU stream) and an unequal latency pass (first 8 pages vs all pages).

corrections.claimed_speedup: kvenanzi/ocr leaderboard pages/s vs EasyOCR: 3.47 vs 1.11 on G4 (3.1x derived) is tail-dominated; per-track G4 books 7.39 vs 0.69 but stress 1.22 vs 1.26; EasyOCR faster per page on G4, A100 and L4; PaddleOCR 3 faster (4.13 pages/s on G4).
corrections.caveats: Track smaller than one batch (2 x workers = 96 on G4), stress track dominates wall time; 8-48 processes vs one GPU stream; latency pass times first 8 pages per track for Tesseract only; pytesseract reloads eng+fra+deu+lat per page; distro Tesseract 5.3.4, flags unstated; 0-star single-author harness.

tier_reason: Lowered B to C: the independent OpenCV wiki numbers compare iGPU hardware codecs with a software baseline crippled by the harness (OpenCV 3.4.2's FFmpeg writer never set thread_count, so VP8 and MPEG-2 encoded on one core, and its colour conversion ran single-threaded inside the timer while the GStreamer pipeline used 4 convert threads); per the crippled-baseline rule the measurement is first-party-grade at best.

corrections.claimed_speedup: OpenCV wiki (2018, i5-6600): gst-vaapi H.264 encode 193 vs 51 fps and VP8 10.3x over OpenCV's FFmpeg backend, with the FFmpeg side single-threaded for VP8 and MPEG-2 and no hardware path; gst-vaapi slower on every mkv decode.
corrections.caveats: Hardware vs software codecs; baseline single-threaded by harness default; videoconvert n-threads=4 vs single-threaded sws_scale; 1000 identical SMPTE frames, output unchecked, write-only timer; gstreamer-vaapi removed 2025-06-10 in favour of the va plugin; OpenCV 4.x FFmpeg backend now has VAAPI.
